summary.text: Matt Koleszar is a Democratic state representative from Michigan's District 22, first elected in 2018, who is the Democratic candidate for Michigan State Senate District 5 in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A former high school social studies teacher, he chaired the House Education Committee in 2023-2024.

paragraphs.text: Matt Koleszar was born in Michigan.
He earned a bachelor's degree in history teacher education from Saginaw Valley State University in 2006 and a master's degree in English studies from Eastern Michigan University in 2011.
His career experience includes working as a high school social studies teacher with Airport Community Schools.
Koleszar has served in the Michigan House of Representatives since 2019 and is not seeking re-election to District 22 in 2026.
In the 2025-2026 session he was assigned to the Education, Elections and Ethics, and Transportation committees, and he chaired the Education Committee in 2023-2024.
He advanced from the Democratic primary for State Senate District 5 on August 4, 2026.
In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, Koleszar described himself as a public school teacher of 12 years and said he was the lead sponsor of Michigan's distracted driving law.
He also said he sponsored a fix to the Police and Fire Survivors' tuition grant so that children of officers and firefighters who die in the line of duty can attend college tuition-free in Michigan.
